quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Kids building a snow fort during a school break"?
quests.hint: Think about when children are usually outside playing during a break from school.
quests.explanation: Yes! Playing outside in the snow is usually a daytime activity.
quests.funFact: A well-packed snow fort can take a whole afternoon of teamwork to build!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A winter sky, early darkness settling in long before dinner is finished"?
quests.hint: Think about what 'darkness settling in' tells you about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! Darkness settling in means night has already begun, even if dinner isn't quite done.
quests.funFact: In winter, the sun sets much earlier, so it can get dark before dinnertime!

quests.instruction: "A field trip to an orchard during the crisp autumn air" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when school field trips are usually scheduled.
quests.explanation: Yes! School field trips happen during school hours, in the daytime.
quests.funFact: Apples are usually harvested in autumn, once they've had all summer to ripen!

quests.instruction: "Fall leaves rustling outside as a family watches a movie indoors" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when families usually settle in together to watch a movie.
quests.explanation: Yes! Family movie time usually happens in the evening.
quests.funFact: Movie night is a cozy tradition that many families enjoy together each week!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "Children splashing through puddles left by a spring shower". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when children are usually outside playing after a rain shower.
quests.explanation: Yes! Playing outside after a shower is usually a daytime activity.
quests.funFact: Puddle-jumping is a favorite springtime activity for kids all over the world!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A cool spring breeze slipping through a cracked window at bedtime". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about when a cracked window would let in a cool breeze right before sleep.
quests.explanation: Yes! A breeze felt right before bedtime means it's already nighttime.
quests.funFact: A cool breeze at bedtime can help a bedroom feel just right for sleeping!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A summer camp group hiking a sunny forest trail"?
quests.hint: Think about when a summer camp group would be out hiking together.
quests.explanation: Yes! A sunny forest trail is a clear sign it's daytime.
quests.funFact: Hiking is a great way for campers to explore nature and get exercise together!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Fireflies blinking over a summer lawn as families relax on porches"?
quests.hint: Think about when fireflies actually blink brightly enough to notice.
quests.explanation: Yes! Fireflies blink most noticeably once it's dark, at night.
quests.funFact: Fireflies are actually a type of beetle, not a fly at all!

quests.instruction: "Leaves crunching underfoot as a class walks to the library" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when a class would walk together to the library during school.
quests.explanation: Yes! A class walking to the library happens during school hours, in the daytime.
quests.funFact: Fallen leaves crunch because they've dried out and lost their water!

quests.instruction: "A thick winter blanket pulled up high against the evening chill" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when the chill of the day really starts to set in.
quests.explanation: Yes! Evening leads into night, when a thick blanket feels extra cozy.
quests.funFact: Heavier blankets can trap more warm air, which helps you stay toasty on cold nights!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A garden bursting with spring tulips near the playground". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when children would be near the playground to notice the tulips.
quests.explanation: Yes! Children are usually near the playground during the day.
quests.funFact: Tulip bulbs need a cold winter before they can bloom brightly in spring!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "Crickets singing louder as a warm summer evening deepens into full dark". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about the phrase 'deepens into full dark' — what does that tell you?
quests.explanation: Yes! Full dark means night has arrived.
quests.funFact: You can guess the temperature outside by counting how fast crickets are chirping!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "Kids racing to grab the last popsicle from the freezer on a hot summer afternoon"?
quests.hint: Think about when a hot, sunny day would make a cold popsicle sound extra good.
quests.explanation: Yes! A hot day calling for a popsicle points to daytime.
quests.funFact: Popsicles were invented completely by accident, by an 11-year-old boy!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A family gathered by a fireplace on the year's very first cold evening"?
quests.hint: Think about when a fireplace would be lit and glowing warm for a family gathering.
quests.explanation: Yes! Evening leads into night, a cozy time to gather by a fireplace.
quests.funFact: Fireplaces have been used to warm homes for thousands of years!

quests.instruction: "A scarecrow standing watch over a field of ripening corn" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when birds are usually flying around fields, which is why scarecrows are needed.
quests.explanation: Yes! Scarecrows are meant to guard fields during the day, when birds are active.
quests.funFact: Scarecrows have been used by farmers for thousands of years to protect their crops!

quests.instruction: "Frost forming quietly on a windowpane while the house sleeps" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when the air outside gets cold enough for frost to form.
quests.explanation: Yes! Frost forms overnight, as temperatures drop after dark.
quests.funFact: Frost forms when water vapor in the air freezes directly onto a cold surface!

quests.instruction: You notice this happening: "A backpack tossed by the door, muddy sneakers kicked off, and the smell of fresh-baked cookies cooling on the counter". What time of day is it?
quests.hint: Think about all three clues together: a backpack, muddy shoes, and cookies — what do they suggest happened right before?
quests.explanation: Yes! This scene suggests someone just got home from school in the afternoon, part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: The smell of baking cookies comes from a reaction between sugar and flour called caramelization!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A nightstand lamp glowing warm, a book closed, and quiet breathing filling the room"?
quests.hint: Think about all three clues together: a lamp, a closed book, and quiet breathing.
quests.explanation: Yes! A glowing lamp, a finished book, and quiet breathing all suggest someone has just fallen asleep at night.
quests.funFact: A warm, dim lamp is often used at bedtime because bright light can make it harder to fall asleep!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The hum of a lawnmower nearby, plus the bright red of a stop sign glinting in the light"?
quests.hint: Think about both clues together: a lawnmower running, and a sign glinting in visible light.
quests.explanation: Yes! A running lawnmower and a glinting stop sign both point to daytime.
quests.funFact: Stop signs are painted a bright color specifically so drivers notice them quickly!

quests.instruction: "The hum of a fan, a pile of blankets pulled high, and the porch light glowing outside" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about all three clues together — a humming fan, blankets, and a glowing porch light.
quests.explanation: Yes! A glowing porch light and blankets pulled high both point to nighttime.
quests.funFact: A gentle fan hum is sometimes called 'white noise,' and it can help some people sleep more soundly!

quests.instruction: "A whistle blowing to start a soccer match, with parents cheering from the sidelines" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when youth soccer matches are usually scheduled.
quests.explanation: Yes! Youth soccer matches are usually played during the day.
quests.funFact: Soccer is played and loved by people in nearly every country in the world!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "A whistle-quiet street, a single cat crossing under a lamp, and every shop shuttered". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about all three clues together: a quiet street, a lamp, and closed shops.
quests.explanation: Yes! A quiet street with closed shops and a glowing lamp all point to nighttime.
quests.funFact: Many shops close for the night and reopen again the next morning!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "The click of a seatbelt, a backpack on a lap, and a school building coming into view". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about all three clues together — where is this trip heading?
quests.explanation: Yes! Heading toward school with a backpack means it's morning, part of the daytime.
quests.funFact: Many families have a set morning routine to help the day start smoothly!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "The click of a seatbelt loosened, a yawning driver, and headlights cutting through fog long after the moon has risen"?
quests.hint: Think about the phrase 'after the moon has risen' — that's a strong clue about the time.
quests.explanation: Yes! The moon having already risen tells you it's nighttime.
quests.funFact: Headlights are especially important for safe driving once it's dark outside!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A line of ants marching past a dropped ice cream cone on a hot sidewalk"?
quests.hint: Think about when sidewalks get hot enough to notice, and when ice cream is usually enjoyed outside.
quests.explanation: Yes! A hot sidewalk and a dropped ice cream cone both point to a sunny daytime scene.
quests.funFact: Ants can carry objects many times heavier than their own body weight!

quests.instruction: "A trail of ants pausing near a porch light, drawn by its steady glow" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when a porch light would actually be switched on and glowing.
quests.explanation: Yes! A glowing porch light means it's dark outside, so it's nighttime.
quests.funFact: Some insects are drawn toward light, which is why bugs often gather near lamps after dark!

quests.instruction: "The rustle of pages as a class reads together, quiet except for a ticking wall clock" — when does this happen?
quests.hint: Think about when a whole class would be reading together in a classroom.
quests.explanation: Yes! A class reading together happens during school hours, in the daytime.
quests.funFact: Reading together as a class can help students learn new words and ideas from each other!

quests.instruction: Think about this: "The rustle of pages as a bedtime story is read, quiet except for a ticking clock on the shelf". Does it happen in the Daytime or the Nighttime?
quests.hint: Think about when a story like this is usually read, right before sleep.
quests.explanation: Yes! A bedtime story is read at night, right before sleep.
quests.funFact: Reading together at bedtime is a cozy tradition enjoyed by families everywhere!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A whistle at recess and a sudden rush of sneakers across the blacktop"?
quests.hint: Think about when recess happens during the school schedule.
quests.explanation: Yes! A recess whistle sends everyone rushing outside during the school day.
quests.funFact: A recess whistle is often used to signal that it's time to line up and head back inside!

quests.instruction: When do we see or do this: "A whistle far off in the distance and the rumble of a late freight train"?
quests.hint: Think about when trains might rumble by with barely anyone around to hear.
quests.explanation: Yes! A late freight train suggests it's already nighttime.
quests.funFact: Many freight trains travel through the night to deliver goods across long distances!
